archetype: Five-colour legendary-permanent toolbox. strategic_frame.json calls it exactly that, and the audit agrees by declining to name an archetype at all — base targets apply, so every template figure below is a starting point rather than a verdict. The deck's currency is access: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain is a repeatable, self-escalating battlefield tutor whose gate widens as the board's colour count grows.
verdict: The mana works and the commander lands: 93.5% turn-3 land drops, zero unconditional taplands, commander cast a mean 2.963 and 99.1% by turn 6. What limits the deck is conversion. threat-density counts three finishers and none of Boros Charm, Kambal or Samut closes three opponents; the only checker-passed kill in the deck is stack 002's Najeela + Derevi combat loop, which needs {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every single combat — the same five-pip, zero-generic cost Sisay's own activation needs. One resource gates both the engine and the only verified win, and some of the deck's own mana is barred from supplying it: Sol Ring makes colourless, and mana_analysis names Delighted Halfling and Unclaimed Territory as restricted to casting spells, which an activated ability is not.

open_questions.question: Can a legend Sisay puts onto the battlefield this turn be tapped to pay for the next activation — via Relic of Legends' cost, or via the '{T}: Add one mana of any color' Esika grants it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the deck chains fetches inside one turn or across two, which is the difference between a tutor and an engine. Stack 003 argues Relic works and Esika's grant does not, but its checker verdict is fail on the iteration bound, so nothing here is fact.

open_questions.question: Does Mikaeus, the Lunarch arrive as a 0/0 and die immediately when put onto the battlefield by Sisay rather than cast, since X is never chosen?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Mikaeus is one of only three mana value 1 or less legendary permanents in the deck. If he is not a live target at Sisay's base power 2, the cold-start pool is two cards, not three, and the opening-turn sequencing advice changes.

open_questions.question: Should the 'Sisay online with a three-colour legend to grow her' target be re-declared as any two legendary permanents of differing colours?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Sisay's power counts distinct colours among OTHER legendary permanents, and 33 of them qualify — the declared four-card group is one shortcut to power 5, not the requirement. Its 52.5% assembled rate is currently the thinnest figure in the audit, and it may be measuring the wrong question.

open_questions.question: Which face does Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge enter on when Sisay puts it onto the battlefield rather than casting it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: cards.json gives the front face as mono-green and The Prismatic Bridge side as all five colours. If a fetched copy could arrive on the Bridge side it would be a second one-card route to power 7 alongside Jodah; on the front face it advances the ladder by a single rung. It also decides whether the card is a five-colour mana source when fetched, which is the binding engine component.

open_questions.question: Do Jodah, the Unifier's anthem and Flowering of the White Tree's +2/+1 stack on top of the colour count to raise Sisay's power beyond 7?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The colour arithmetic alone already puts the structural ceiling at power 7 and the gate at mana value 6, so this is no longer about whether the ladder exceeds power 6 — it does. It is about how far above 6 a future addition could sit and still be fetchable.

open_questions.question: Does Najeela plus a single omni-mana body — Faeburrow Elder, Esika, or Selvala, Heart of the Wilds — loop without Derevi?

No archetype is established, so every axis target is a base template rather than a fitted one. strategy:deckbuilding.ratios is explicit that its counts should come from the deck's actual failure modes.

upgrade-facts' synergy channel returned only ramp:cost-reduction cards for this deck and surfaced no candidate for the thinnest engine component. The channel is a format-wide top-10 shortlist, not a fit score, and it found nothing usable here.

The obsolescence index proposes Elvish Mystic as an upgrade to both Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder on similarity 0.9755 and 0.9667. It is format-agnostic and does not know that this deck buys those two cards for five-colour output, not for a green mana; the recommendation is wrong and is recorded here rather than acted on.
DECK_ROLE_BUDGET's shortfalls (draw 4, sweeper 2, tutor 1, wincon 1) are labelled provisional and uncited by upgrade-facts itself and were not used as evidence anywhere above.
The deck has no sideboard, so every add is a pool proposal with no owned-card evidence behind it.

The ladder's top rung is empty and nothing here prices it. Sisay reaches mana value 6 at five distinct colours among other legends, and the deck's highest nonland mana value is 5. Whether a mana value 6 legendary permanent earns a slot depends on how often five colours is actually reached, which no artifact measures — the declared goldfish targets stop at 'a three-colour legend'.

findings.note: "She is legendary at mana value 4, so unlike every other draw engine here Sisay can actually go and get her" is false, and the same sentence names its own counterexample. Reki, the History of Kamigawa is in cards.json at {2}{G}, mana value 3, Legendary Creature, "Whenever you cast a legendary spell, draw a card" — a draw engine, legendary, and fetchable at Sisay power 4 (gate is mana value LESS THAN power), a strictly LOWER rung than Jhoira's mana value 4 / power 5. The entry itself says "Reki already does the legendary half" two clauses earlier. Five more in-deck legendary draw pieces are also fetchable: Kutzil (mv 3), Loran of the Third Path (mv 3), Selvala, Heart of the Wilds (mv 3), Rona (mv 2) and Sheoldred (mv 4), plus Teferi, Time Raveler (mv 3). This also contradicts axes[5].reading of this same document, which names Loran, Kutzil, Kenrith and Teferi as showing draw in oracle text — all legendary, all fetchable. The claim does not merely overstate, it points the wrong way: Jhoira is the LEAST fetchable of the deck's legendary draw engines, sitting one rung above Reki. The redundancy argument beside it (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors, "So stack the classes you want every game (ramp, draw, removal, enablers), tutor only the irreplaceable") is quoted verbatim and in context and would carry the add on its own; the fetchability differentiator is the part a reader would act on and it is untrue. add_candidates is byte-identical to the committed version, so this survived the previous pass rather than being introduced by the fix.

The re-argument is sound and the Kenrith correction landed. cost_of_cutting now reads "it returns the creature under its OWNER's control, so in practice it is a rebuy of your own dead body and not a way to take an opponent's" — matches cards.json oracle exactly: "{4}{B}: Put target creature card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under its owner's control." difficulty is still contested. why is verified line by line: Kenrith is mv 5 needing Sisay power 6; exactly five LEGENDARY permanents sit at mv 5 (Jegantha, Jodah, Kenrith, Samut, Surrak) — I recomputed the legendary-permanent curve and got {0:1, 1:2, 2:7, 3:14, 4:5, 5:5}, correctly excluding Seedborn Muse, which is mv 5 but not legendary; Kenrith is mono-white and contributes one colour against Jodah's five and Surrak's three. The {R}-mode redundancy claim is new relative to HEAD (it had been listed as a COST) and the migration is justified: Najeela's activation reads "They gain trample, lifelink, and haste until end of turn", quoted verbatim, so within the one checker-passed kill Kenrith's {R} adds nothing. Only observation not rising to a finding: "the smallest of the three losses; that flexibility is the real loss" has an ambiguous antecedent — the three losses are enumerable (graveyard reach, modality, mana sink) but a reader could take "that flexibility" to mean the {4}{B} mode just downgraded.

No incomplete fix. Programmatic sweep of every string field: exactly three describe the {4}{B} mode — axes[11].reading, cut_candidates[0].cost_of_cutting, cut_candidates[4].cost_of_cutting — and all three now say "under its owner's control". No fourth occurrence and no surviving "steals from any graveyard".
